cards.explanation: The answer is the Spirit of the LORD. The text says, "Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah…" (Judges 11:29). After that, he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, then through Mizpah of Gilead. From there he advanced against the Ammonites, friends.

The answer is whatever comes out his door to greet him. Jephthah says, "…whatever comes out the door of my house to greet me on my triumphant return from the Ammonites will belong to the LORD…" (Judges 11:31). Notice how open that wording is, friends. He doesn't name what it will be. I think it's worth slowing down on that line, because the story leans on it.

The answer is True. The text says, "So Jephthah crossed over to the Ammonites to fight against them, and the LORD delivered them into his hand." (Judges 11:32). That's the very thing Jephthah's "If indeed" was asking for, friends. The part of the vow that depended on the win has now happened.

The answer is daughter. The text says, "…there was his daughter coming out to meet him with tambourines and dancing!" (Judges 11:34). She came out to meet him, friends. I think this is where the story gets heavy, so let's take the next part gently.

The answer is False. "She was his only child; he had no son or daughter besides her." (Judges 11:34). The verse takes a moment to say so, friends, and I think that tells us how much is on the line. This one is heavy.

The answer is that he gave his word to the LORD. Jephthah says, "…for I have given my word to the LORD and cannot take it back." (Judges 11:35). His vow in verse 30 was made to the LORD, friends. I think this one hurts, so let's go slowly.

The answer is that the LORD avenged him of the Ammonites. She says, "you have given your word to the LORD. Do to me as you have said, for the LORD has avenged you of your enemies, the Ammonites." (Judges 11:36). She starts with the vow and then points to what the LORD just did, friends. I think it's quite a moment, and what she says is remarkable.
The answer is friends. She asks to wander "…through the mountains with my friends…" (Judges 11:37). She doesn't ask to go alone, bakers. I think there's something tender in that.
The answer is False. Jephthah answers her request with one word: "Go," and he sends her away for two months (Judges 11:38). She leaves with her friends, friends. I think that one word carries a lot.
The answer is mourn. The text says she "…mourned her virginity upon the mountains." (Judges 11:38). She left with her friends to do it, bakers. I think we should let that sit for a moment.

The answer is that young women lament his daughter four days a year. The text says it "has become a custom in Israel that each year the young women of Israel go out for four days to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite." (Judges 11:39-40). Her story wasn't forgotten, friends. I think that's the heaviest line in the whole passage.
